interactables.title: Municipal Ordinance 404
interactables.text:
NOTICE TO CITIZENS:
Any resident discovering that their house, spouse, or childhood never existed must file Form 88-A before sundown. Unregistered nostalgia is punishable by a five-crown fine.

Residents who discover they themselves never existed should not file anything, as they lack standing. - By order, Royal Bureau of Records

interactables.title: Bellwether Census, Spring Posting
interactables.text:
HOUSEHOLDS OF BELLWETHER (PARISH COPY)

Kettleburn, M. (innkeeper, no kin recorded)
Vaelen, quartermaster (licensed)
Fenwick, librarian (two cats, unlicensed)
Oakhaven, clerk (Bureau)

The next line has been scraped from the board with a knife. The wood beneath it is pale and new, the way skin is under a scab. Your fingers find the grooves of letters that are no longer there, and for one dizzy moment they feel like your own name.

interactables.title: WANTED - By Order of the Royal Bureau of Records
interactables.text:
WANTED: SABRINO, called "the Italian Witch"

CHARGES:
- 1,412 counts of Unlicensed Fireballing
- Arson of a Cheese Wheel of Historical Significance (the Great Wheel of Vallo, aged 90 years, now aged 0)
- Impersonating a Royal Chef
- Impersonating a Royal Chef while on fire
- Crimes against the Edrath Accords of Polite Warfare (extensive; see attached ledger, 4 volumes)
- Teaching a goose to cast Ember Bolt

Sabrino is armed with a very tall hat and is extremely charming. DO NOT accept dinner invitations. Do not accept second helpings. Do NOT ask about the goose.

REWARD: 500 crowns, payable upon submission of Form 13-S (Witch, Apprehended) in triplicate.

Scrawled across the bottom in a cheerful hand: "Grazie for the lovely portrait! You got my good side. - S."

interactables.title: CONTRACTS (Monster Hunters Only. That Means You, Baggy.)
interactables.text:
CONTRACT: Something haunts Hollowmere Manor, south of the village. Reward: 200 crowns. Previous hunters: 6. Returned: 2. One of them was a horse.

CONTRACT: Bring me ten wolf pelts. NOTE: wolves in this region carry, on average, 0.3 pelts each. Some carry none. Science has no explanation. Bring a big bag.

CONTRACT: Escort my uncle to the Old Road. He walks slightly slower than you walk and slightly faster than you sneak. He will stop to talk to every goat. Do not let him talk to the goat.

CONTRACT: I have lost my grandmother's amulet. It is somewhere on the continent. Please hurry.

CONTRACT: There are rats in the cellar. Crossed out. Underneath, in different ink: 'it's always rats'. Underneath that: 'why is it always rats'. Underneath that, in Vaelen's handwriting: 'please'.

WANTED: Card players. Must not cheat. Must not mind losing to a man who cheats. - H.

interactables.title: NOTICE from the Church of the Last Dawn
interactables.text:
To the owner of the HORSE currently standing on the chapel roof:

Please collect your horse.

Nobody saw it get up there. There is no way up there. It is not stuck. It is not distressed. It is simply standing on the ridge of the roof, facing slightly to the left, chewing, and every so often it vanishes for a moment and reappears exactly where it was.

Brother Aldous has blessed it twice. The blessing did not stack.

If it is yours, it answers to 'Trout'. Apparently.

interactables.prompt: Pick Up the Torn Script Page
interactables.title: THE TRAGEDIE OF THE UNCOUNTED KING - Page One
interactables.text:
ACT ONE, SCENE ONE. The inside of a great ledger.

NARRATOR: Once there was a King whom all the world forgot. Not by war, nor plague, nor the slow grey dust of years, but by a single stroke of ink.

KING (waking): Who struck my name? Who dares to strike a king?

SECOND GUARD: Who goes there?

KING: I do! Your King!

SECOND GUARD: ...Who?

[In spidery red ink, in the margin: 'The guard's line is the best in the scene. This is not a compliment to the guard. One star. - M.Q.']

[Below, in pencil, in a different hand: 'Filed under FICTION, UNLICENSED. - O.']

interactables.title: CASTING CALL!
interactables.text:
THE VELOUR TRAVELLING PLAYERS
proudly present
THE TRAGEDIE OF THE UNCOUNTED KING

A play in five acts. Two intervals. One dragon.

NOW CASTING: a LEAD (must have suffered), a PRINCE (must own sword), a GHOST (must be pale), a DRAGON (must be large), a HERALD, a NARRATOR, a SECOND GUARD (there is no First Guard; budget), a PROMPTER, and someone who is not afraid of fire, or the law.

No experience required. No pay guaranteed. Glory almost certain.

Apply to Madame Odette Velour, in person, in the large hat.

Underneath, in red ink: 'Two stars. The font is overwrought. - M.Q.'

interactables.title: Form 1-CS: Character Sheets (Thursday Group)
interactables.text:
A neat stack of character sheets, every one filled out on official Bureau Form 1-CS.

SIR DETECTIVE INSPECTOR BAGGINGTON. Paladin of Justice. Equipment: magnifying glass (+1), eleven spare magnifying glasses, a hat. Notes: 'Suspects the hedge.'

GERALD. Human. Accountant. Equipment: abacus, cardigan (+3 AC, knitted). Notes: 'Wants to audit the dragon.'

GRIZZLEBEARD. Monster hunter. White hair. Two swords. Says 'hmm'. All attributes listed as 18. In pencil, in Oakhaven's hand: 'NO.'

LORD DEFINITELY-NOT-A-VAMPIRE. Paladin. Avoids sunlight 'for unrelated reasons'. Backstory: see attached, 41 pages.

SISTER CRUMB. Cleric. Heals with bread. Spell list: 'bread'. Notes: 'Brings real snacks. Protect at all costs.'

Under the stack, a blank sheet with your name already written at the top in neat Bureau handwriting, as if somebody hoped you'd say yes.

interactables.prompt: Look at the Hoofprints on the Wall
interactables.title: Hoofprints, Going Up
interactables.text:
Muddy hoofprints cross the grass, stop at the library wall, and then simply keep going: straight up the wall, across the roof tiles, along the ridge, and down the far side, where they continue across the square as if nothing unusual has happened.

Somebody, probably Brother Aldous, has chalked a little halo round each one, "in case it was a miracle".

Underneath, in Fenwick's handwriting: "It wasn't a miracle. It was a horse. Please stop chalking my wall."

interactables.title: A Smear of Glowing Ink
interactables.text:
A smear of something that glows faintly green on the Records Office step, like a footprint. You dab it with a finger. It's luminous ink, the expensive kind they sell in Saltmere. It comes off on your hand.

Ghosts, as far as you know, don't leave footprints. And they certainly don't buy ink.

interactables.title: A Crumpled Receipt
interactables.text:
A receipt, screwed up and thrown into the alley:

SALTMERE DRAPERS & SUNDRIES
1 x bedsheet, extra large, white ... 6 silver
1 x jar luminous ink ... 1 gold
1 x 'Ghost-B-Gone' charms, crate of 200 ... 40 gold (NO REFUNDS)
Paid in full. Thank you, V.

The 'V' is underlined twice.

interactables.title: A Box Behind the Market Stall
interactables.text:
Behind the market stall, half-hidden under a tarpaulin: an empty crate stencilled GHOST-B-GONE, a pot of glue, and a stack of new price tags.

The old tags say 1 SILVER. The new tags say 5 GOLD. The dates on them are the morning after the Phantom Clerk first appeared.

interactables.title: The Trap
interactables.text: (The trap is set.)

interactables.title: Boundary Marker of the Third Reign
interactables.text:
"Here stood the market-borough of Oakhallow, population 412."

Beneath the chiseled letters, someone has scratched in fresh charcoal: "There is only forest here. Why do I remember the baker's daughter?"

interactables.title: Field Journal of Kaelen, Ashbound
interactables.text:
Day 41. The boundary stone of Oakhallow again. Four hundred and twelve souls, it says. I count the foundations in the bracken: none. I count the wells: one, dry, with a bucket still on the rope.

Day 43. The Annex has sunk. Its upper offices fell into something older underneath, and the stairs now go down further than the building ever went up. The skeletons inside still keep office hours.

Day 44. A traveller from Bellwether asked what we Ashbound are for. I told her: somebody has to remember things on purpose.

interactables.title: CASE FILE #1: THE MISSING TOWN
interactables.text:
Property of BAGGY, Private Eye (Licence pending. Licence fee also pending.)

SUSPECTS:
1. The hedge. Too neat. Hiding something.
2. The Bureau. Too many forms. Hiding EVERYTHING.
3. A goat. (Probably not involved. Looked at me funny.)
4. Myself? (Ruled out. I have an alibi: I was here. Wait.)

CLUES:
- Boundary stone says 412 people. I count 0 people. Discrepancy of 412. Very large discrepancy.
- One dry well. One bucket. Somebody was thirsty, once.
- I remember a girl with flour on her nose who gave me a sweet roll. I was seven. Nobody else remembers her. CENTRAL MYSTERY.

THEORY: A whole town was erased by someone with very good handwriting.

NEXT STEPS: Find the town. Find the girl. Find my other glove.

interactables.title: A Note, Weighed Down with a Clove of Garlic
interactables.text:
To Whoever Finds My Hat,

The Bureau is onto me again. They have charged me with 1,412 counts of Unlicensed Fireballing, which is a lie. It was 1,413. They always forget the one at the wedding.

I am leaving the hat and my good grimoire here under the pine, because a witch on the run cannot also carry a hat that tall. It keeps catching on tavern doors. Very bad for a dramatic exit.

Take them. Wear the hat crooked, it works better. Cast the fireball from FAR away. Further than that. No, further.

And if a nice man in a long coat asks where I went, tell him dinner is at eight, as always, and he is still invited.

Ciao,
Sabrino

P.S. Do not let anyone tell you that pineapple goes on anything. That is the real war crime.

interactables.prompt: Pick Up the Torn Script Page
interactables.title: THE TRAGEDIE OF THE UNCOUNTED KING - Page Two
interactables.text:
ACT TWO, SCENE ONE. A haunted battlement. Moonlight.

PRINCE VALIANT: Spectre! Release the King!

GHOST OF THE OLD KING: Never! For I too was forgotten, and I will not be forgotten alone!

PRINCE VALIANT: Then have at thee!

(They duel. It goes on for some time.)

(It goes on for a bit longer.)

[Margin, red ink: 'These two are clearly in love. The playwright appears to be the only person in the audience who has not noticed. - M.Q.']

The page has been nailed to a pine tree, at exactly the height of a critic's top hat.

interactables.prompt: Look Up at the Top of the Stone
interactables.title: On Top of the Boundary Stone
interactables.text:
Eleven feet up, on the very top of the boundary stone, where nothing larger than a crow could possibly perch, there is a neat, fresh pile of horse manure.

It is still steaming.

There are no hoofprints anywhere round the base of the stone. There are no hoofprints on the stone. There is just the evidence, on top, steaming, defying every law of nature and several of the Bureau's.

interactables.title: The Figure It Out Wagon
interactables.text:
Painted along the side in enormous wobbly letters, between the flowers:

THE FIGURE IT OUT GANG
Mysteries Solved! Monsters Unmasked! Reasonable Rates!

Underneath, in smaller letters, added later: "Not responsible for traps."

Underneath THAT, smaller still, in Karma's handwriting: "Bread is responsible for traps."

interactables.title: A Hat on a Stick
interactables.text:
In the ditch beside the road: a broom handle with a battered felt hat nailed to the top. Seen from a distance, at night, through a visor, it would look exactly like a knight's plume.

Or a hat on a stick. Which is what it is.

Karma is going to be unbearable about this.

interactables.title: A Hand-Painted Sign
interactables.text:
A wooden board, propped against a rock, painted in big careful letters:

TOLL ROAD
PAY THE HEDLESS KNIGHT
5 GOLD
(OR 4)
(THIS IS NOT A BANDIT THING)

The 'A' in HEADLESS has been added later, above, with a little arrow.

interactables.title: A Receipt in the Verge
interactables.text:
VAELEN'S PROVISIONS & ODDITIES
1 x suit of plate armour, used, slightly haunted (the haunting is free) ... 30 gold
Customer is paying in instalments of 1 gold.
Customer has paid 1 gold.
Sold to: S.

On the back, in different handwriting: 'cut hole in top for my head. hat on stick. DONT FORGET THE STICK'

interactables.title: The Trap
interactables.text: (The trap is set.)

interactables.prompt: Lower Crypt Portcullis (Controlled by Archive Lever)
Sealed Royal Vault Gate (Step on Rune Plate)

interactables.title: Chief Archivist Morvath's Log
interactables.text:
"The portcullis to the lower crypt answers to the iron lever in the eastern archive. Should the King's inquisitors ever breach this hall, the Royal Treasury gate to the north opens only when weight is placed upon the rune-plate in the north-west corner."

Later, the hand less steady: "Struck Oakhallow tonight. Four hundred and twelve. I wrote every name myself. If anyone ever comes to undo this, let them know it was not done lightly. I am binding myself to the Ledger. Nothing will take it from me. Nothing."

interactables.title: Census of Oakhallow, Folio III (Struck)
interactables.text:
MARKET-BOROUGH OF OAKHALLOW, POP. 412

...Brannock, Tomas. Baker. Ovens on Mill Lane.
Brannock, Marta. Elder daughter, aged seventeen. Apprenticed to the bakehouse.
Brannock, Ilse. Younger daughter, aged nine.

Every line on the page has been struck through in red ink, all but one. Beside Ilse's name, in a neat archivist's hand:

"Moved to Vault III for safekeeping. Elder sister relocated to Bellwether, memory sealed. God forgive us. - M."

interactables.title: Annex III Duty Roster
interactables.text:
NIGHT WATCH - VAULT III (THE NURSERY)

Sister Hessa Vane, Night-Warden - every night. Do not relieve her. She will not be relieved.
Chief Archivist Morvath - the Ledger. Do not disturb him. He has stopped sleeping.
W. Ashcombe, Junior Archivist - lamps, filing, and NOT misfiling.

REMINDER TO ALL STAFF: the children's names are NOT to be spoken aloud inside the Annex, not even as a kindness. Especially not as a kindness.

Tea rota cancelled until further notice.

interactables.prompt: Pick Up the Torn Script Page
interactables.title: THE TRAGEDIE OF THE UNCOUNTED KING - Page Three
interactables.text:
ACT THREE, SCENE ONE. A mountain. Red light.

NARRATOR: And from the mountain came the Dragon, and the Dragon spoke.

THE DRAGON: ROAR!!!

KING: Foul worm! I am not afraid!

THE DRAGON: ROAR!!!

KING: Still not afraid!

THE DRAGON: ...roar.

[Margin, red ink, underlined three times: 'NEEDS A DRAGON. A BETTER ONE. - M.Q.']

Someone, probably a Bone Clerk, has stamped the page RECEIVED and filed it between two tax returns.

interactables.title: Held in Trust
interactables.text:
Under a pane of clouded glass lies a girl of nine, breathing slow as winter. Flour still dusts one sleeve.

A brass plate on the lid: I. BRANNOCK. HELD IN TRUST UNTIL SAFE.

Seventeen years, and she has not aged a day. Her lips move in her sleep, shaping the same word over and over, the way you repeat a thing so as not to forget it.

The word is "Marta".

interactables.title: The Night-Warden's Lullaby
interactables.text:
Hush, little names, the ink is deep,
the Hunger walks but cannot keep
what no one speaks and no one knows.
Sleep in the ledger. Sleep in the snows.

Hush, little names, till morning comes,
till someone signs the Seal for sums
of all the souls we hid below.
Until then, sleep. And I will not go.

In the margin, in a shaking hand: "Morning never comes. Morvath has stopped coming down. I sing anyway. If I stop singing, they wake, and if they wake, the Hunger hears them. - H.V."

interactables.prompt: Pick Up the Torn Script Page
interactables.title: THE TRAGEDIE OF THE UNCOUNTED KING - Page Four
interactables.text:
ACT FOUR, SCENE ONE. A nursery, in the dark.

HERALD: Hear ye! Hear ye! The King is not dead!

NARRATOR: But the King was tired, so very tired, and the night was long, and somewhere a lullaby was playing.

KING: Then let me sleep a little. But wake me. Promise you will wake me. Promise you will say my name.

[Margin, red ink, much smaller than the others: 'This scene should not be set here. Not in this room. Not with these children asleep. - M.Q.' And beneath it, fainter: 'But it is good.']

interactables.title: Here Lies...
interactables.text:
Here lies GROGNAK THE MIGHTY.
Strength 18. Intelligence 3.
He tried to intimidate a door. The door won.

interactables.title: Here Lies...
interactables.text:
Here lies SIR REGINALD, who split the party.
"You lot take the left corridor, I'll be fine."
He was not fine.

interactables.title: Here Lies...
interactables.text:
Here lies ELARA MOONWHISPER SHADOWBLADE NIGHTSONG,
last of her clan, orphaned twice, cursed thrice.
Her tragic backstory ran to fourteen pages. The game master read two.

interactables.title: Here Lies...
interactables.text:
Here lies the BARD, who rolled to seduce the dragon.
It was a natural 20.
The dragon has not stopped writing letters.

interactables.title: Here Lies...
interactables.text:
Here lies PIP THE QUICK, rogue,
who checked the chest for traps.
The chest was the trap. It had teeth.

interactables.title: Here Lies...
interactables.text:
Here lies BRANDT, who stepped on the same pressure plate four times
to see if it would still do that.
It still did that.

interactables.title: Here Lies...
interactables.text:
Here lies a GNOME, name unknown, who ate an amulet
because it was 'probably food'.
It was an amulet of strangulation. It was not food.

interactables.title: Here Lies...
interactables.text:
Here lies a HERO who saved the realm, the king, the princess and a goat,
then spent eleven hours deciding what to put in the stash.
He died of old age at the chest. The goat lived.

interactables.title: Here Lies...
interactables.text:
Here lies a MONSTER HUNTER who swore he'd finish the contract
right after one more hand of cards.
That was nine years ago. The monster died of old age.

interactables.title: Here Lies...
interactables.text:
Here lies TOMAS THE SAVE-SCUMMER.
He reloaded so many times the world grew suspicious.
On the last attempt, the world reloaded him.

interactables.title: The Lawn of Ill-Advised Choices
interactables.text:
A small, cheerful sign planted in the grass:

"MEMORIAL LAWN for Adventurers Who Came Before You.
Please don't loot the graves.
We KNOW you're going to loot the graves.
They're empty. The previous adventurers looted them."

- P. Hollowmere

interactables.title: Hollowmere Manor - Private Grounds
interactables.text:
HOLLOWMERE MANOR
Home of Sir Percival Hollowmere, Bart., Host of the Finest Parties in the Marches

Underneath, carved later and much less neatly:

"YOU MUST GATHER YOUR PARTY BEFORE VENTURING FORTH."

And under that, in fresh chalk: "we tried. nobody came. - P."

interactables.title: A Mournful Wail
interactables.text:
A long, heartbroken wail rolls across the garden and makes the hairs on your neck stand up. It is exactly the kind of noise a Banshee is supposed to make.

It is also exactly the kind of noise a very large, very sad dog would make.

You note it down as evidence. Probably.

interactables.prompt: Kitchen Back Door (it's open; it's always open; that's the problem)

interactables.title: EVIDENCE BOARD (Property of Hollis)
interactables.text:
Somebody has set up a chalkboard in the foyer, like a hunter's wagon parked outside a haunting.

EVIDENCE FOUND:
[ ] Cold spots
[ ] Ghost writing
[ ] Floating objects
[ ] Spirit box response
[ ] Ectoplasm handprints
[ ] Wailing

RULES:
1. Find three kinds of evidence.
2. Check the Field Guide.
3. Do NOT say its name out loud. Especially not in the dark. Especially not as a joke.
4. If the lights start flickering, that's normal. If they start flickering in Morse code, leave.
5. Do not hide in the wardrobe. It always finds you in the wardrobe.

interactables.prompt: Inspect the Figure in the Hall
interactables.title: A Figure in the Hall
interactables.text:
A mannequin stands in the corner of the foyer, arms stuck rigidly straight out to either side, legs together, face perfectly blank.

It has been standing like that for weeks, the butler's diary says. It doesn't move. It doesn't attack. It just stands there in that pose, as if it is waiting for somebody, somewhere, to finish loading its animations.

You back away slowly. Its arms do not follow you. You're almost disappointed.

interactables.title: The Table Is Laid
interactables.text:
The long table is laid for twelve. Silver, crystal, folded napkins shaped like swans.

As you watch, a fork lifts itself off the tablecloth, turns slowly in the air, and settles back down a finger's width to the left, exactly in line with its neighbours. Then a spoon does the same. Then a whole place setting shuffles over to make room for a guest who isn't there.

FLOATING OBJECTS. Somebody is setting the table. Somebody who has been setting it for a very long time.

interactables.prompt: Sideboard Drawer (labelled 'STUDY KEY - DO NOT LOOK HERE')

interactables.title: Hollowmere Library: Most Borrowed
interactables.text:
A brass placard: MOST BORROWED THIS CENTURY.

1. 'Dusk' - A girl moves to a rainy town and falls for a three-hundred-year-old who still attends school, on purpose.
2. 'Moon of Longing' - The sequel. The same girl, but now a wolf with abs is also involved. Nobody wears a shirt.
3. 'A Lament of Frost and Furnace, Vol. 6' - The author promises Vol. 7 'soon'. The placard is very old.
4. 'The Boy Who Was Prophesied' - Seven volumes. The prophecy turns out to be about a different boy.
5. 'The Fellowship of the Very Long Walk' - Three hundred pages of walking. Twelve of fighting. Forty of songs.
6. 'Fifty Shades of Grey Robes' - An archivist romance. Fenwick has borrowed it eleven times. Fenwick denies this.
7. 'So You've Been Chosen' - A self-help pamphlet for farm boys with mysterious birthmarks.

Somebody has written 'TEAM ROLF' in the margin of the second book, and 'TEAM ASHGRAVE' beneath it, and the two have been arguing in the margins for several pages.

interactables.title: You Search for Treasure
interactables.text:
You search the library for treasure.

You find... nothing.

Somewhere, a deep and booming voice you can't quite place adds, with enormous satisfaction: "A WANDERING MONSTER APPEARS."

No monster appears. The voice sounds disappointed.

interactables.prompt: Read the Rulebook on the Floor
interactables.title: Page 212 of a Very Thick Rulebook
interactables.text:
A heavy rulebook lies open, its margins crowded with arguments in at least six different hands.

"Technically, page 212 says a crossbow can be fired while falling." - "It does NOT say that." - "It doesn't say you CAN'T." - "We are not doing this again." - "I cast Fireball on the rules discussion." - "You can't, you're a Fighter." - "Page 212."

Someone has drawn a very small, very sad dragon at the bottom, with a speech bubble: "can we please just play."

interactables.title: Claw Marks on the Back Door Frame
interactables.text:
Deep gouges, four at a time, scored into the frame of the kitchen's back door at about head height.

Something big came in this way. Something with claws, that walks on two legs, that apparently also wiped its feet on the mat afterwards, because the mat is spotless.

It LOOKS like evidence. You note it down.

interactables.title: A Cold Spot
interactables.text:
You step into the middle of the dance floor and your breath turns to frost in front of your face. It is much, much colder here than anywhere else in the room. The cold has a shape: a little circle, the size of one person standing still, waiting to be asked to dance.

COLD SPOTS. You write it down with fingers that have gone stiff.

interactables.title: The Gramophone
interactables.text:
A beautiful brass gramophone with a horn like a lily. The record on it is labelled 'For My Guests - The Last Waltz'.

You wind it. It plays four bars of a waltz, skips, and plays the same four bars again. And again. Somewhere above you, very faintly, something hums along.

interactables.prompt: Pick Up the Torn Script Page
interactables.title: THE TRAGEDIE OF THE UNCOUNTED KING - Page Five
interactables.text:
ACT FOUR, SCENE TWO. The Bureau.

KING: Though the ledger strike my name, though the ink run dry, though every clerk in every hall forget that I was I...

(The rest of the speech has been torn away.)

[Margin, red ink: 'I have kept the rest. If the Velour woman wants it, she may come and fetch it herself. Or send someone braver. I shall be in the library. I am always in the library. - M.Q.']

As you finish reading, the temperature in the library drops, and between two bookshelves, a thin figure in a top hat lowers a book and looks at you over it.

interactables.prompt: Sealed Room (a lever somewhere opens this)

interactables.title: Sherry Decanters, Bitten
interactables.text:
A row of crystal decanters on the dresser. Every one of them has two neat little puncture holes in the stopper, as if someone tried to drink through them with their teeth.

They all contain beetroot juice.

It LOOKS like evidence. You note it down, slightly confused.

interactables.title: Sir Percival's Guest Book
interactables.text:
A leather guest book lies open on the desk with a quill beside it. The last hundred pages are blank, every one of them headed with a date, as if waiting for signatures that never came.

While you watch, the quill lifts on its own, dips itself in the ink, and writes in a looping, old-fashioned hand:

    you came    you came    please stay for dinner

GHOST WRITING. Your hand is shaking a little as you note it down.

interactables.prompt: Read the Note by the Lever
interactables.title: A Note from the Architect
interactables.text:
"To whomever it may concern:

There was going to be a puzzle here. Four rotating busts, a riddle about the seasons, and a sliding-tile mural of Sir Percival's prize hound.

After the third guest starved to death trying to solve it, Sir Percival asked us to take it out. The lever opens the sealed room. That's it. That's the whole puzzle. You're welcome.

- G. Fairweather, Architect

P.S. The answer to the riddle was 'a candle'. It's always a candle."

interactables.title: The Spirit Trumpet
interactables.text:
A brass speaking-trumpet on a stand, the kind ghost-hunters swear by. You lean in and ask, very politely: "Is anyone here? Give us a sign."

Static.

"Where are you?"

Static.

"How old are you?"

A long pause. Then, very faintly, from somewhere downstairs: four bars of a waltz, skipping.

No voice. No answer. NOT spirit box evidence, then. Whatever lives here doesn't want to chat through a trumpet. It wants company.

interactables.title: Portrait: Sir Percival at Thirty
interactables.text: A handsome young man in a velvet coat, laughing, a glass raised. The plaque reads: 'Host of the Year, eleven years running.' In the background of the painting, a crowded ballroom.

interactables.title: Portrait: Sir Percival at Sixty
interactables.text: The same man, older, still smiling. The ballroom behind him is half empty. The painter has been very kind about it.

interactables.title: Portrait: Sir Percival at Ninety
interactables.text: An old man sitting alone at a very long table laid for twelve. He is still smiling. The smile has not reached his eyes for some time.

interactables.title: Portrait: A Monster Hunter
interactables.text: A grizzled, white-haired man with two swords, scowling at the painter. The painting is titled 'Hmm.' He is holding a hand of cards behind his back.

interactables.prompt: Read the Note on the Chest
interactables.title: A Note Taped to the Treasure
interactables.text:
"Congratulations on finding the Secret Treasure of Hollowmere!

It's a party hat. I'm sorry. I had it made for my last party. Nobody came, so nobody wore it.

They always say the real treasure is the friends you made along the way. I never made any. Perhaps you could wear it for me, the next time you're somewhere with friends.

- P."

interactables.title: Pawprints in the Soil
interactables.text:
Huge pawprints, deep in the soft soil between the marrow beds. Very convincing. Very scary.

Except that pressed into the bottom of every single one is the clear, neat tread of a sandal. A size nine. With a little sun stamped on the heel.

interactables.title: A Scrap Caught on the Fence
interactables.text:
A scrap of rough brown wool caught on a nail in the garden fence. Coarse, hand-woven, the kind used for religious habits.

And a single fake claw, made of painted wood, lying in the grass beneath it.

interactables.title: Bellwether Marrow Show: Previous Results
interactables.text:
Pinned to the potting shed, a list in Rolf's enormous handwriting:

BELLWETHER MARROW SHOW
Year 1: 1st Rolf. 2nd Br. Aldous.
Year 2: 1st Rolf. 2nd Br. Aldous.
Year 3: 1st Rolf. 2nd Br. Aldous.
Year 4: 1st Rolf. 2nd Br. Aldous (protest lodged, dismissed).

At the bottom: "This year's show is next week! Good luck everyone! Especially Aldous! -Rolf"

interactables.title: The Trap
interactables.text: (The trap is set.)

interactables.title: The Drowned Lantern
interactables.text:
THE DROWNED LANTERN
Ales, Chowder, Lodgings
PROP. M. BRINE

Underneath, a smaller sign, newer, nailed on crooked:

"PATRONS ARE KINDLY REMINDED NOT TO SAY THEIR NAMES ON THE PREMISES.
It only encourages it."

interactables.title: Field Notes, Prof. A. Pickering (Collegium, Dept. of Unusual Studies)
interactables.text:
Day 3. The fishermen will not say their names. Not in the tavern, not on the boats, not to their own children. When pressed, one wrote his name on a napkin, then ate the napkin.

Day 4. The tide comes in nine minutes late, every day, and goes out nine minutes early. Something is drinking it.

Day 5. Found a fish-shaped idol in a net. It was warm. It is still warm. It is warm in my pocket now and I do not remember putting it there.

Day 6. I have begun to dream in a language with too many vowels. In the dream I am being counted. The count does not end.

Day 7. Must not say my name. Must not say my name. Must not say my name. Ambrose. Ambrose Pickering. I am Ambrose Pickering. I

interactables.title: Saltmere Tide Ledger
interactables.text:
HIGH WATER / LOW WATER / REMARKS

Mon. - 9 min late. 9 min early. Fair.
Tue. - 9 min late. 9 min early. Fog.
Wed. - 9 min late. 9 min early. Fog. Boats came back one short. Nobody can say who.
Thu. - Fog.
Fri. - The water was counting. Could hear it. One, two, three. Stopped at a number I didn't like.
Sat. - 
Sun. - 

The last two lines are blank except for wet fingerprints, too long, with too many joints.

interactables.title: BY ORDER OF THE HARBOURMASTER
interactables.text:
NOTICE TO ALL VESSELS AND PERSONS:

1. Fishing is permitted between dawn and the fog.
2. Do not fish in the fog.
3. Do not answer if the fog calls you by name.
4. Do not say your name in the fog, in case it is listening.
5. If you hear bells under the water, you did not hear bells under the water.
6. Chowder at the Drowned Lantern, two coppers.

Pinned beneath it, a cheerful pamphlet:

"THE ESOTERIC ORDER OF THE DROWNED LEDGER welcomes NEW MEMBERS! Tired of having a name? Let the Deep carry it for you! Benefits include: eternal life (partial), gills (most members), a lovely robe, and the peace of never being counted again. Meetings: under the fish warehouse, every tide. Bring nothing. Especially not your name."

interactables.prompt: Look at the Horseshoe on the Bollard
interactables.title: A Horseshoe, Dripping
interactables.text:
Somebody has hung a horseshoe on the mooring bollard at the foot of the pier. It is dripping seawater and has a small crab living in it.

Chalked on the bollard, in a fisherman's capitals: "HORSE CAME OUT OF THE SEA TUESDAY. NODDED AT SILAS. WENT BACK IN. NOBODY SAY ANYTHING. IT HAD BETTER MANNERS THAN THE OTHER THING."

Underneath, smaller: "It was heading west. Following a whistle."

interactables.title: Gale & Sons Fish Co. - Shipping Ledger
interactables.text:
CATCH / WEIGHT / BUYER

Cod, 40 lb, the Drowned Lantern
Herring, 112 lb, Bellwether
Names, 9, The Order
Names, 14, The Order
Names, 31, The Order
Names, ALL OF THEM, The Order

The last entry is in a different hand, and the ink is still wet, and it is salt water.

interactables.prompt: Cellar Gate (it smells of the sea)

interactables.title: Tide Bell (First)
interactables.text:
A great bronze bell hangs from a beam, green with age, covered in barnacles that shouldn't grow this deep. It is ringing. Nobody is ringing it. With every stroke, the pool in the middle of the chapel ripples outward, in rings, like something below is listening.

You wrap your coat round the clapper and hold it still until the ringing stops. Your hands are wet afterwards. They stay wet for an hour.

interactables.title: Tide Bell (Second)
interactables.text:
The second bell. Its rim is engraved with names, hundreds of them, so small and so close together that they look like a pattern of scales. Some of the names are very old. Some of them are fresh. One of them, near the bottom, is still being engraved, by nothing, letter by letter.

You stop the bell before it finishes the name. You do not look to see whose it was.

interactables.title: Tide Bell (Third)
interactables.text:
The third bell is small, a ship's bell, polished, the kind that marks the watches on a voyage. It rings eight bells: end of the watch. Then a ninth. Then a tenth. It keeps counting.

You silence it, and in the silence afterwards you hear, from very far below the floor, something enormous turn over in its sleep.

interactables.prompt: Read the Hymn Carved in the Wall
interactables.title: The Drowned Hymn
interactables.text:
Carved deep in the stone, the letters worn by centuries of wet fingers:

    Iä! Iä! N'gahl th'ruun!
    The Name-Eater dreams beneath the tide.
    Speak, and be counted. Be counted, and be eaten.
    Iä! The ledger of the deep is never closed.

    What is written, it can find.
    What is spoken, it can taste.
    What is struck out, it cannot see,
    and what it cannot see, it fears.

The last four lines have been scratched at, furiously, as if someone tried to erase them and couldn't.

interactables.title: THE WHISTLING WOOD
interactables.text:
THE WHISTLING WOOD

Named for the wind in the Old Oak, which whistles. Visitors are asked not to whistle back. It only encourages it.

Beneath, in a different hand: "WOLVES. Some of them dressed as relatives. Do not let them in."

Beneath that, in a third hand, very small and very shaky: "also there's a horse in my tent. help. - S"

interactables.title: The Old Oak's Hollow
interactables.text:
A knot-hole the size of a fist, low on the trunk, worn smooth. As you lean close, the wind moves through the wood, and the hollow whistles.

Two notes. Low, then high. Sharp and short, the way a man whistles who has done it ten thousand times without thinking.

Somewhere above you, in the branches, something large shifts its weight and snorts, as if answering.

You've heard that whistle before. Outside the Lantern Inn. Across a card table. It's Hollis's.

interactables.prompt: Read the Notes Pinned to the Tree
interactables.title: Crumpled Drafts
interactables.text:
Seven sheets of paper, nailed to a pine one above the other, each one crossed out.

1. "Dear Sir. I have your horse. Sorry."
2. "WE have your horse." (There is only one person here.)
3. "WE HAVE YOUR HORSE."
4. "WE HAV YOUR HORS." (Margin note: more frightening if spelled wrong? check with night school)
5. "300 gold or you will never see her again." (Margin note: he will though. she keeps turning up. on the TENT.)
6. "Please come and get your horse."
7. "PLEASE come and get your horse she has eaten all my carrots and she was in the soup."

On the back of every sheet, faintly, the printed grid of a Lantern Inn character sheet.

interactables.prompt: Read the Note on the Bed
interactables.title: A Note, in Grandmotherly Handwriting
interactables.text:
"To whoever finds this:

I have gone to live with my sister in Saltmere, where there are no wolves, only the unspeakable horrors of the deep, which at least have the decency not to wear your clothes.

The wolf is wearing my second-best nightgown. If you see him, tell him the bonnet does not suit him and it never did.

The red hood is in the wardrobe. My granddaughter has given up on it. She does archery now. She is very good. The wolf knows.

Love, Granny

P.S. A horse has been standing on my roof for two days. It is a very polite horse. I left it a carrot."

interactables.prompt: Read the Plaque by the Door
interactables.title: The Saltmere Light
interactables.text:
SALTMERE LIGHT
Raised in the Year of the Long Tide by the Fishermen's Guild
"So that every boat comes home, and every name with it."

KEEPERS: J. Marsh. P. Marsh. E. Marsh. O. Marsh.

The last name has no end date. Below it, scratched with something sharp, a tally of days: so many that they cover the bottom of the plaque, the doorframe, and the first yard of the tower wall.

interactables.title: Log of the Saltmere Light, O. Marsh
interactables.text:
"Day 1. Father's gone. I keep the light now. It's not hard. Trim the wick, fill the oil, wind the clock. And never let it go out."

"Day 900. Father said the light isn't for ships. It's for the thing under the reef. While it can see the light, it dreams. While it dreams, it isn't hungry. I thought he was joking. He wasn't."

"Day 20,000 (I think). I died some time ago. I've kept the light anyway. Nobody has come to relieve me. I don't mind. Somebody has to."

"Day ?. The men in robes came and sang, and the light went out. It has never gone out. I can't relight it. My hands go through the matches now. I need someone who's still solid. I need someone it can't see."

interactables.title: A Name in a Bottle: THOMAS GALE
interactables.text:
A green bottle, stoppered with wax, wedged between two rocks. Inside, a strip of sailcloth with a name stitched on it in red thread, the stitches small and careful, the kind a mother makes:

THOMAS GALE

Underneath, in smaller stitches: "Eldest. Bad at knots. Good at laughing."

It feels warm in your hand. It feels like it's been waiting.

interactables.title: A Name in a Bottle: ABEL GALE
interactables.text:
A brown bottle, half buried in sand. Inside, a page torn from a school primer, the alphabet down one side and, in a child's enormous letters, practised over and over until the page ran out:

ABEL GALE  ABEL GALE  ABEL GALE  ABEL GALE

At the bottom, in an adult hand: "He was so proud when he could write it. -S."

interactables.title: A Name in a Bottle: BARTHOLOMEW FENN
interactables.text:
A bottle with a ship in it. A very small ship. On the deck of the very small ship, a very small man is holding up a very small fish, triumphantly. The label reads:

BARTHOLOMEW 'BART' FENN
Wanted to be remembered as the man who caught the Big One. Caught it. It ate him. Remember him anyway.

interactables.title: A Name in a Bottle: GRANNY WEATHERBY
interactables.text:
A jam jar. The label still says 'DAMSON, LAST SUMMER'. Inside, a recipe card:

GRANNY WEATHERBY'S CHOWDER
(Do not tell Brine. Brine thinks hers is better. Brine is wrong.)

The recipe is long, specific, and ends with: "...and a pinch of salt for every name you love. Use a lot of salt."

interactables.title: A Name in a Bottle: (blank)
interactables.text:
A clear glass bottle, very old, the glass gone milky with salt. There's a slip of paper inside. You shake it out.

It's blank.

Not faded. Blank. Somebody put a name in here once, and the sea took the name and left the paper, and sent the paper home anyway, because the sea, for all its hunger, has a sense of form.

You keep the paper. It seems wrong not to. Nobody should be nobody.

interactables.title: A Name in a Bottle: ONDINE MARSH
interactables.text:
A lamp-glass, of all things, the chimney off an old oil lamp, stoppered at both ends with cork. Inside, a lock of grey hair tied with string, and a label in a neat, tired hand:

ONDINE MARSH. Keeper.

"If anyone finds this, I was here. I kept the light. Please tell somebody."

interactables.title: A Very Expensive Sign
interactables.text:
A sign of polished mahogany with gold-leaf letters:

THE LATE CINDERMAW
Private Residence of G. Quillsby, Esq.
NO DRAGONS
NO CLERKS
NO VISITORS
(This means you.)

Someone has painted over 'LATE' in red and written 'VERY MUCH ALIVE'. The brushstrokes look like they were made with a claw.

interactables.title: Cushion Inventory (Partial)
interactables.text:
CUSHIONS, SILK: 1,200
CUSHIONS, VELVET: 340
CUSHIONS, 'FOR SITTING ON CUSHIONS': 12
CUSHION, ONE (1), EMBROIDERED 'GRUBNIK IS A GOOD BOY': 1, a gift from Mother

Total: 2,104 gold of the dragon's money, and not one chair in the house.

interactables.title: The Shoe Room
interactables.text:
Racks and racks of tiny shoes, floor to ceiling: buckled, beribboned, patent leather, one pair entirely of gold with little ruby toes. Each pair has a label: 'TUESDAY', 'COURT', 'GLOATING', 'GLOATING (FORMAL)'.

Three hundred pairs. Kobolds have four toes. These were all made to measure. The cobbler's bill alone was worth a small village.

interactables.prompt: Read the Letter on the Desk
interactables.title: A Letter, Half-Written
interactables.text:
To the Royal Bureau of Records, Name Change Department

Dear Sirs,

I wish to formally change my name from Grubnik Quillsby to Cindermaw the Elder, as the previous holder of the name is legally deceased and will not be needing it. I enclose the fee (eleven gold, one sheep, one apology).

P.S. Please also transfer the title 'Terror of the Eastern Mountains'.

[The letter stops. There's a large ink blot, as if the writer heard something enormous land outside.]

interactables.prompt: Recover the Missing Third of the Hoard
Look at the Marks on the Wall
interactables.title: Handprints in Old Flour
interactables.text:
Small handprints, a child's, pressed into the stone in old flour. They lead along the wall to a gap where the masonry has been opened, and a stair going down: deeper than the Annex was ever built.

Someone has chalked beside them, in an archivist's neat hand: "VAULT III. THE NURSERY. DO NOT WAKE."

interactables.prompt: Read the Scratches on the Wall
interactables.title: Scratched into the Stone
interactables.text:
Dozens of hands have cut the same words into the wall, over and over, in different scripts and different centuries:

TURN BACK. THE NAMES ARE LISTENING.

Beneath them, newer and neater, in Bureau ink: "Graffiti is a Class III municipal offence."
